```plato

    //==
    // # Ear clipping
    //
    // A convex corner whose triangle holds no other vertex is an EAR: clipping it
    // emits one face and leaves a simple ring one vertex shorter, so a ring of n
    // vertices yields n - 2 faces.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polygon_triangulation#Ear_clipping_method
    //
    // The cost of the pass is the ear test, and it is paid per candidate: the test
    // below walks the ring, so the pass is O(n^2). The obvious speed-up — caching
    // convexity and a blocker count on each node, refreshing only the clipped ear's
    // two neighbours — is UNSOUND, and quietly so. Clipping can flip a neighbour
    // from reflex to convex, and a vertex that stops being reflex stops blocking
    // every candidate whose triangle it sat in, not only the two nodes the clip is
    // local to. Those counts go stale, real ears stop being recognised, and the
    // pass falls through to its degenerate-input path and emits OVERLAPPING
    // triangles. A cache has to invalidate on the reflex/convex flip, not on
    // adjacency; until one does, this stays a plain scan.
    // Style: see STYLE_GUIDE.md - API-first and geometry priority (correct first;
    // a faster variant is separate, later work).

    // True when no vertex of the ring lies inside the corner at `slot`. Only reflex
    // vertices are tested: a convex vertex of a simple ring lies outside every
    // other corner's triangle. The corner's own neighbours are skipped — they are
    // its triangle's endpoints.
    HasNoBlocker(points: Array<Point2D>, nodes: Buffer<EarClipNode>, slot: Integer): Boolean
    {
        var a = nodes.At(slot).Prev;
        var c = nodes.At(slot).Next;
        var q = nodes.At(c).Next;
        var blocked = false;
        while (q != a && blocked.Not)
        {
            blocked = points.CornerTurn(nodes, q) <= 0.0
                && points.BlocksEar(nodes, q, a, slot, c);
            q = nodes.At(q).Next;
        }
        return blocked.Not;
    }

    // Corner `slot` is an EAR when it turns counter-clockwise and no other ring
    // vertex lies inside its triangle.
    IsEar(points: Array<Point2D>, nodes: Buffer<EarClipNode>, slot: Integer): Boolean
        => points.CornerTurn(nodes, slot) > 0.0 && points.HasNoBlocker(nodes, slot);

    // The next corner to clip, searching from `cursor`: the first ear, or — when
    // the input violates its declared invariants and no ear exists — the first
    // convex corner, which keeps the pass terminating. -1 when neither exists.
    FindEar(points: Array<Point2D>, nodes: Buffer<EarClipNode>,
        cursor: Integer, remaining: Integer): Integer
    {
        var ear = -1;
        var slot = cursor;
        var visited = 0;
        while (visited < remaining && ear < 0)
        {
            if (points.IsEar(nodes, slot)) { ear = slot; }
            slot = nodes.At(slot).Next;
            visited = visited + 1;
        }
        if (ear < 0)
        {
            slot = cursor;
            visited = 0;
            while (visited < remaining && ear < 0)
            {
                if (points.CornerTurn(nodes, slot) > 0.0) { ear = slot; }
                slot = nodes.At(slot).Next;
                visited = visited + 1;
            }
        }
        return ear;
    }

    // The face at the corner `slot`, over pool indices.
    CornerFace(slot: Integer, nodes: Buffer<EarClipNode>): TriangleFace
        => TriangleFace(nodes.At(nodes.At(slot).Prev).Vertex, nodes.At(slot).Vertex,
            nodes.At(nodes.At(slot).Next).Vertex);

    // Clips the ring through `head` down to its last triangle and returns the faces
    // in clipping order. Consumes the buffer. A head of -1, or a ring shorter than
    // a triangle, yields no faces.
    ClipEars(points: Array<Point2D>, nodes: Buffer<EarClipNode>,
        head: Integer): Array<TriangleFace>
    {
        var faces = new List<TriangleFace>();
        var live = nodes;
        var remaining = head < 0 ? 0 : head.RingLength(live);
        var cursor = head;
        while (remaining > 3)
        {
            var ear = points.FindEar(live, cursor, remaining);
            if (ear < 0)
            {
                remaining = 0;
            }
            else
            {
                var next = live.At(ear).Next;
                faces = faces.Add(ear.CornerFace(live));
                live = ear.Unlink(live);
                remaining = remaining - 1;
                cursor = next;
            }
        }
        // The nesting is load-bearing: `&&` is `And`, an ordinary function of two
        // already-evaluated arguments, so it does NOT short-circuit. Written as one
        // condition, the walk below would run even for an empty ring, where
        // `cursor` is -1.
        if (remaining == 3)
        {
            var last = live.At(cursor).Next;
            if (points.CornerTurn(live, last) > 0.0)
            {
                faces = faces.Add(last.CornerFace(live));
            }
        }
        return faces.Freeze();
    }

    // The faces of one pool of points carrying an outer ring and zero or more
    // holes: every ring linked and cleaned, every hole bridged in, then one
    // clipping pass. The kernel every entry point below is written against.
    TriangulateRings(points: Array<Point2D>, holeStarts: Array<Integer>): Array<TriangleFace>
    {
        var capacity = points.Count + holeStarts.Count * 2;
        var nodes = new Buffer<EarClipNode>(capacity);
        var r = 0;
        while (r < holeStarts.RingCount)
        {
            var start = holeStarts.RingStart(r);
            var end = holeStarts.RingEnd(r, points.Count);
            var area = points.RangeSignedArea(start, end);
            nodes = start.LinkRing(nodes, end - start, r == 0 ? area > 0.0 : area < 0.0);
            nodes = points.FilterRing(nodes, start, end);
            r = r + 1;
        }
        nodes = points.BridgeHoles(nodes, holeStarts);
        nodes = points.FilterRing(nodes, 0, capacity);
        var head = 0.FirstLiveSlot(nodes, capacity);
        return points.ClipEars(nodes, head);
    }

    //==
    // # The IMesh2D obligations
    //
    // Faces index the same points the caller passed in, so a triangulation can be
    // traced back to the ring it came from.

    // The polygon triangulated over its own vertices, by ear clipping.
    Triangulate(p: Polygon2D): TriangleMesh2D
        => (p.Points, p.Points.TriangulateRings(0.Range));

    // The convex polygon triangulated over its own vertices. Convexity makes every
    // corner an ear, so the fan from the first vertex is already a triangulation
    // and no clipping pass is needed.
    Triangulate(p: ConvexPolygon2D): TriangleMesh2D
        => (p.Points, (p.Points.Count - 2).MapRange(i
            => TriangleFace(VertexIndex(0), VertexIndex(i + 1), VertexIndex(i + 2))));
```
